transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?

Taking care of my mom on top of work has thrown my whole life off, and I feel like I’m not handling any of it the way I usually would. It just feels like everything is piling up, and I'm really struggling to keep my head above water.
How long have you been feeling this way, and did these struggles begin around the time you took on these caregiving responsibilities?

These struggles have been going on for about four months now, ever since my mom had her stroke and I became her main caregiver. It all started within just a few weeks of her stroke, right as I began juggling her hospital visits and care with my shifts at the shop. It has just been an overwhelming grind ever since.
Have you lost interest or pleasure in the things you normally enjoy, or is your distress mainly focused on the stress of managing your mom's care and work?

It's definitely the overwhelming stress of trying to balance my mom's care with my job. I haven't lost interest in the things I love, but I've had to stop going to church and my classic truck club because I'm just running on fumes. I'm completely exhausted and simply don't have the time or energy for them right now.

Do you find yourself constantly worrying about many different areas of your life, even minor things, or is your anxiety mostly focused on your mother's health and managing your daily responsibilities?

It's definitely focused on my mom's health and trying to juggle her care with my job at the shop. I don't really worry about random minor things, but I'm constantly terrified I'm going to mess up her meds or get fired because I'm so distracted. It just feels like my mind is completely consumed by trying to manage this crisis.
Would you say your distress is mostly felt as constant anxiety and tension about managing everything, or are you also experiencing a persistent low, sad, or hopeless mood?

Honestly, it’s really a mix of both. I feel this constant, heavy tension and anxiety about dropping the ball at work or with my mom's care, but I also experience moments of deep sadness where I end up crying in the restroom at the shop and pulling away from everyone.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your sleep patterns or your appetite since this situation started?

My sleep has definitely been affected; I lie awake at night beating myself up over dropping balls at home and at work. As for my appetite, I haven't really noticed any big changes, mostly because I'm just too busy and exhausted to pay much attention to it.
Have you had any thoughts of wishing you were dead, or thoughts of hurting yourself in any way during this difficult time?
No, I haven't had any thoughts like that at all. Even though I'm incredibly overwhelmed and exhausted right now, I've never wanted to hurt myself or wished I was dead.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient exhibits mixed anxiety and depressive symptoms (tension, worry, crying spells, social withdrawal, and insomnia) that directly developed within weeks of a clear psychosocial stressor (his mother's stroke and the sudden burden of caregiving). The symptoms have lasted for four months and cause significant functional impairment (stopping church and club activities, distraction at work), but they do not meet the full diagnostic criteria for a major depressive episode or generalized anxiety disorder.
